title: Marabouts et Khouan: etude sur l'Islam en Algerie, ch. XX (Khelouatya): extracts from the order's books after Shaykh al-Sanusi, on dhikr, khalwa visions and the seventy thousand lights
author: Louis Rinn, translating Muhammad b. 'Ali al-Sanusi (d. 1859) on the Khalwatiyya; also quoting 'Abd al-Wahhab al-Sha'rani (d. 1565)
translator: Louis Rinn and the Algerian government interpreters (Arabic to French)
edition_cited: Alger: Adolphe Jourdan, 1884; archive.org maraboutsetkhoua00rinn (OCR text)
tradition: Khalwatiyya / Rahmaniyya (North Africa); also other Algerian orders
locator_hints: Ch. XX 'Ordre des Khelouatya', printed pp. 293-302 (OCR lines ~14443-15430)

summary: A French colonial survey of Algerian Sufi orders that prints long translated extracts from the orders' own manuals. The Khalwati chapter gives, after al-Sanusi, the seated posture and the head movement of the la ilaha illa'llah dhikr, the series of Names taken up one at a time on the shaykh's word, and a description of what the adept sees: apparitions come only in solitude after long devotions; first the light of ablutions and prayers, then a demonic light, then forms; then seventy thousand lights distributed over seven degrees, each with its colour and a condition for seeing it (for the red lights, food must be stripped of what one most craves, or they appear dulled by smoke, in which case one should go no further). It also quotes Sha'rani's criticism that such visions are products of exhaustion.
why_relevant: A public-domain rendering of an order's working description of coloured lights in khalwa, with conditions, sequence, a stop rule and an internal critique.
